# Draft PDF adapter provenance and integration

`full_draft_pdf.py` is imported from the standalone reader reconciliation fix1 source snapshot. Original source SHA-256: `ca424e20c6ad3ba4fc044248dbf98d8c6ebf32c80e2fbc6d8e2301e348cd59cf`. The worker calls its `print_source` function with the staged reader, staged report and expected immutable report digest, then uses its existing isolated browser profile and atomic installation flow. `Dockerfile` copies this vendor directory into the worker image; `pypdf==6.21.4` supports the PDF annotation regression.

The adapter prints a version-matched companion index with relative paths and hashes, and makes recognized source links internal destinations. Evidence bytes are not embedded; obtain the matching package separately. Unknown links have their targets removed. The output remains a pending-review draft. The full integrated PDF has not received every-page reading-size, physical keyboard, screen-reader or production viewer review. Do not infer review approval or publication.

The earlier source snapshot was tested on RAY: 45 pages, zero URI annotations, 250 resolving named links and 210/210 selected text items; all-page contact sheets were reviewed only at reduced size. Backend workflow tests independently exercise the current worker with a local synthetic/historical fixture and Chromium, including digest-bound input, URI absence, destination resolution and the index disclaimer. Run `python -m pytest tests/test_pdf_export.py tests/test_workflow.py` with `SCOOBY_BROWSER` pointing to an installed Chromium executable to exercise the PDF path.

A subsequent local print-layout correction lets long cards split while keeping summary cards and pillar headings together. The fixture PDF was rechecked for empty pages; no report or evidence bytes change. All-page reading-size and target-viewer review remain open.
